stories.title: Civilian casualties climb as Russia and Ukraine exchange fresh strikes
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine traded fresh strikes overnight, with Moscow targeting Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk. Ukraine retaliated with a drone attack on Russia’s Voronezh region. Falling debris set fire to a Wildberries warehouse. Ukraine’s military said it also struck a Russian oil refinery in Orsk. The exchange of strikes comes after a deadly weekend of attacks, with civilian casualties mounting on both sides.

stories.title: Bulgaria drone crash a wake-up call for country's defenses
stories.summary: The explosion of a Ukrainian decoy drone in Bulgaria near the Romanian border reveals gaps in Bulgaria's defenses, raises questions and shines a light on the country's policy shift on the war in Ukraine.
stories.post: 📰 NEWS: Bulgaria drone crash a wake-up call for country's defenses. The explosion of a Ukrainian decoy drone in Bulgaria near the Romanian border reveals gaps in Bulgaria's defenses, raises questions and shines a light on the country's policy shift on. Source: DW World.
article_sentences: When a drone entered Bulgaria's airspace on Saturday and exploded in a sunflower field near the northeastern village of Kardam — about 100 meters (328 feet) from a border checkpoint with Romania — the immediate question was where the aircraft had come from.
Following an on-site check, the Bulgarian Defense Ministry said the drone was a Ukrainian-manufactured Maya decoy aircraft used to activate and deceive enemy drone systems.

And while both Bulgarian and Ukrainian officials confirmed that the first drone explosion on Bulgarian territory since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 was in no way deliberate, the case quickly became politically charged.
The Bulgarian Foreign Ministry summoned Ukraine's ambassador on Monday and stressed that "any unauthorized entry into Bulgarian airspace is unacceptable."
Kyiv promised to cooperate fully in clarifying the circumstances of the incident.
What is known about the incident?
At 8:10 a.m.
local time on Saturday, a blast was heard by a police patrol near the Kardam checkpoint on the border between Bulgaria and Romania.
Police and military units cordoned off the area once the exact location of the fallen drone was established in a field.

In his first statement on the matter, Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said there had been neither casualties nor damage to infrastructure but claimed that the drone had been carrying a "significant amount of explosives."
Officials on the ground painted a less dramatic picture, saying the explosion did not even create a crater and that only a few sunflowers had been damaged.

The drone crashed about a kilometer (0.6 miles) from Bulgaria's compressor station on the Trans-Balkan gas pipeline route, which connects Turkey and Ukraine, and in close proximity to a Romanian station.

stories.title: Somali denied World Cup ‘proud’ to referee PSG vs Villa in UEFA Super Cup
stories.summary: Omar Artan was turned away on arrival at Miami International Airport before World Cup 2026 where he was to officiate.
stories.post: 📰 NEWS: Somali denied World Cup ‘proud’ to referee PSG vs Villa in UEFA Super Cup. Omar Artan was turned away on arrival at Miami International Airport before World Cup 2026 where he was to officiate. Source: Al Jazeera.
article_sentences: Omar Artan was turned away on arrival at Miami International Airport before World Cup 2026 where he was to officiate.

Somali referee Omar Artan, who was denied the chance to referee at the World Cup after being refused entry to the United States, will take charge of the UEFA Super Cup between Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) and Aston Villa on Wednesday.

Before the World Cup started in June, the 34-year-old referee unwittingly found himself in the media spotlight after being turned away on arrival at Miami International Airport, despite being part of the panel of referees selected by FIFA for the tournament.
“It was a very tough period,” Artan said in an interview published on the UEFA website.
“A lot of people have sympathy for me, because when someone has been working a lot of years and is supposed to do something, and then can’t do it, it’s very challenging.”

A US Department of State official told the AFP news agency that the referee was “associated with suspected members of terrorist organisations”, therefore “making the traveller ineligible for admission to the United States”.
These allegations were rejected by the referee and caused outrage in Somalia, where Artan had been welcomed as a hero on his return.
“It is unfortunate what happened to the referee from Somalia,” FIFA President Gianni Infantino said at the time, adding: “We don’t control everything.”

In response, UEFA, the governing body of European football, announced that Artan would referee the UEFA Super Cup, which pits Champions League winners PSG against the Europa League winners Aston Villa.
“I was lucky, but I have worked very hard to be here and I’m really proud,” Artan told UEFA.
“As you can imagine, I grew up in a difficult situation, but it didn’t prevent me from pursuing my dreams.”
The first Somali to officiate at the Africa Cup of Nations in 2024, Artan is now set to referee his first match in Europe.
